thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Edge Higher, With Techs Eyeing A New Record

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Edge Higher, With Techs Eyeing A New Record
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Twitter, Apple, Mylan all stocks in focus for Tuesday
U.S. stock futures were rising modestly on Tuesday, with technology shares poised to potentially lead the gains again on the heels of the Nasdaq's first record finish in months.
A smattering of economic data is en route, including the Institute for Supply Management's nonmanufacturing survey. Meanwhile, shares of Twitter Inc. were climbing in premarket trading on news the social media company's stock will now be part of the S&P 500 index.
What are markets doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 27 points, or 0.1%, to 24,823, while S&P 500 index futures inched up 3.25 points, or 0.1%, to 2,748.50. Nasdaq-100 futures gained 12.75 points, or 0.2%, to 7,160.75.
On Monday, the Nasdaq Composite closed at a record (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-street-poised-for-higher-open-as-jobs-optimism-outweighs-trade-fears-2018-06-04) for the first time since March 12, rising 0.7%, to 7,606.46. The S&P 500 finished 0.5%, to 2,746.87, while, the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 178.48 points, or 0.7%, to 24,813.69.
Read:Techs lead buyback boom, on track to put trillions back into investor hands (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tech-leads-stock-market-buyback-boom-with-companies-on-track-to-put-trillions-back-in-investor-hands-2018-06-04)
The Russell 2000 also closed at a fresh all-time high, rising 0.3%, to 1,653.37.
What was driving the market?
Investors were hunting for fresh catalysts to keep the start-of-the-week gains for stocks going, as they regroup after recent market upheaval triggered by political stress in Italy. More stability on that front could be coming, if the new Italian coalition government makes it past a confidence vote in parliament.
Some inspiration may come from the technology sector, given the gains for the Nasdaq Monday. Apple Inc. shares were higher in premarket trading, after scoring a record finish on Monday, as details from its software-focused Worldwide Developer Conference emerged. A rise for Twitter shares was also playing its part. In Tuesday trade, European tech stocks hit a 17-year high, according to Factset.
Investors appeared to be putting trade tensions aside, even after trade talks broke down between the U.S. and China over the weekend. But leaders of the Group of Seven nations will hold talks in Canada on Friday and Saturday, where tariffs and trade are likely to be discussed. This weekend's rebuke by G-7 finance ministers of the Trump administration's trade tariffs could add some stress to the gathering.
Read:Death knell for the G-7 may be at hand after hostile reaction to Trump tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/death-knell-for-the-g-7-may-be-at-hand-after-hostile-reaction-to-trump-tariffs-2018-06-04)
What are strategists saying?
"So far, investors remain focused on a broader subset of U.S. economic data, while concluding that U.S. earnings and the economy are sufficiently robust to keep the equity bull market intact. And for now, putting the prospects of higher U.S. interest rates and global trade wars, which usually scare investors stiff, on the back burner," said Stephen Innes, senior trader with OANDA.
Which stocks were in focus?
Mylan NV(MYL) shares surged 6% in premarket after the drugmaker received Food and Drug Administration approval (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mylan-rallies-on-fda-approval-of-biotech-drug-similar-to-amgens-2018-06-04) for a drug similar to one made by Amgen Inc.(AMGN).
Twitter (TWTR) shares jumped over 3% in premarket trading after S&P Dow Jones Indices announced the microblogging platform's stock would join the S&P 500 index (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/twitter-shares-rise-on-announced-addition-to-sp-500-2018-06-04).
Shares of Apple Inc.(AAPL) could be active. Among the company's WWDC announcements were new augmented-reality development tools and software upgrades for all its products, along with a new Apple Watch and Mac.
See:Apple's WWDC: Blocks on Facebook sharing surprise, but no lift to $1 trillion market cap (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-wwdc-no-immediate-catalysts-to-get-to-1-trillion-market-cap-2018-06-04)
Starbucks Corp.(SBUX) could be in focus after its executive chairman, Howard Schultz, said he would step down late Monday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/starbucks-chairman-howard-schultz-to-step-down-2018-06-04).
What's on the economic calendar?
The Markit services purchasing managers index for May will be released at 9:45 a.m. Eastern Time, following by the ISM's services index for May and job openings for April at 10 a.m. Eastern.
Opinion:A new economic indicator is saying there is no sign of a U.S. recession (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/a-new-economic-indicator-is-saying-theres-no-sign-of-a-us-recession-2018-06-05)
See:MarketWatch's economic calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
What are other markets doing?
Asian stocks finished mostly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-give-up-some-of-mondays-gains-2018-06-04), with gains led by China's Shanghai Composite Index , while the Stoxx Europe 600 index rose modestly.
Crude oil was also managing some gains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-claw-back-some-gains-as-global-production-worries-hover-2018-06-05) after settling at the lowest level in nearly two months on Monday. Gold was flat at $1,296.60 an ounce, while the ICE U.S. Dollar Index was also steady at 93.975.
